title: Environmental Specialist
description:
Job Title: Environmental SpecialistJob Category: ConsultingTime Type: Part timeMinimum Clearance Required to Start: SecretEmployee Type: Part-Time On-Call-Long-Term AssignmentPercentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%Type of Travel: Local* * *

The Opportunity:


CACI is seeking a part time on-call Environmental Specialist to provide specialized regulatory and compliance support to NAVSEA Systems Commands (SYSCOM). This role focuses on air quality compliance, petroleum and tank management, and related environmental regulatory interpretation. The selected candidate will help monitor field activity compliance and support SYSCOM field activities by reviewing permits, resolving emergent compliance and environmental issues, assessing Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) tank standards, and advising on National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants/New Source Performance Standards (NESHAP/NSPS) requirements.

This position is ideal for an environmental professional with Clean Air Act or Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL)/tank expertise who thrives in an advisory, mission support environment.

Work 100% virtually while supporting critical SYSCOM environmental readiness needs.

Responsibilities:


  • Assist with monitoring field activity compliance with Federal, state, municipal, and Navy regulations for air quality or tanks.
  • Provide expert support on Clean Air Act or POL/tank compliance.
  • Resolve emergent compliance issues involving Clean Air Act or POL/tank management requirements.
  • Provide ad hoc regulatory interpretation and technical review of environmental permits and permit conditions.
  • Assess permit condition compliance, including Title V permit applicability and marine coating compliance reviews.
  • Deliver requested training, including Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) approval analysis and emission factor determination.
  • Deliver ad hoc technical training and subject matter guidance on air emissions, NESHAP/NSPS applicability, and tank compliance.
  • Provide requested NESHAP and NSPS regulatory interpretation for Shipbuilding and Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE) requirements.
  • Review Authority to Construct (ATC) and Permit to Operate (PTO) applications, including new Title V applicability analysis.
  • Support Inspector General (IG) audit findings for tank systems by researching secondary containment, NFPA tank labeling, SPCC plan compliance, and tank equipment requirements.
  • Interpret environmental regulations and permit conditions to support operational compliance.
  • Troubleshoot environmental issues in Clean Air Act media or POL/tank management.
  • Support the execution of contract requirements, which may include submission of supporting data and metrics and timely completion of written reports to stakeholders, customers, and CACI leadership.
  • Other duties may be assigned in support of contract taskings and mission success.

Qualifications:

Required:


  • Must be a United States Citizen. Must have the ability to obtain a DOD Interim Secret security clearance prior to start and subsequent final DOD Secret security clearance.
  • Experience in one of the following: environmental engineering, environmental protection, biology, general engineering, tank compliance, or Clean Air Act compliance.
  • Minimum 8 years of experience in Clean Air Act or POL/tank environmental compliance. Experience as a former regulator or spill response expert is acceptable.
  • Experience interpreting Federal and state environmental regulations and evaluating environmental permits.
  • Ability to deliver training on air compliance topics such as VOC analysis and emission factor determination.
  • Experience evaluating NESHAP/NSPS applicability and reviewing ATC/PTO permit applications.
  • Ability to research and assess tank compliance requirements including SPCC, NFPA labeling, and secondary containment.
  • Strong analytical and regulatory interpretation skills.
  • Ability to work virtually and respond quickly to emergent environmental needs.
  • Strong customer service orientation and written/verbal communication skills with the ability to respectfully engage internal and external customers at all levels in a manner that achieves successful outcomes.
  • Outstanding organizational skills to efficiently manage competing priorities, multiple concurrent taskings, and firm deadlines.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365.

Desired:


  • Active DOD Secret security clearance.
  • Prior military or Navy environmental experience.
  • Experience supporting shipbuilding or industrial environmental compliance programs.
  • Familiarity with Title V permitting, air emissions calculations, and tank/POL compliance frameworks.
  • Experience delivering technical environmental training.


This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. However, this position is representative of positions within CACI that are consistently available. Individuals who apply may also be considered for other positions at CACI.

What You Can Expect:

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Pay Range:

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

Since this position can be worked in more than one location, the range shown is the national average for the position.

The proposed salary range for this position is:

$82,100-$172,400

CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

  • Provide individualized documentation feedback by reviewing new clinician records and conducting spot checks, escalating non-coding issues to appropriate teams.

  • Monitor Epic work queues (charge review, follow-up, claim edit) to ensure timely and accurate charge submissions and reduce claim denials.
  • Collaborate across departments—including CMOs, Clinical Informatics, Risk Adjustment, and Population Health—to enhance documentation practices and system optimization.
  • Participate in specialty and department meetings, identifying trends and delivering targeted education to improve coding and documentation accuracy.
  • Refine Epic documentation tools, including templates, order entries, diagnosis lists, and SmartSets/SmartPhrases, to improve efficiency and accuracy.
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory standards, including Medicare, Medicaid, and AHIMA’s Standards of Ethical Coding, while maintaining expert knowledge of evolving policies.
  • Promote a culture of ethical coding and continuous improvement, supporting clinicians with timely updates, feedback, and education to ensure accurate reimbursement and compliance.

Licensure, Registration, and/or Certification Required:

  • Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA) or Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT) certification, or Coding Specialist (CCS) certification, or Coding Specialist – Physician (CCS-P) certification issued by the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) or Professional Coder (CPC) certification issued by the American Academy of Professional Coders (AAPC). Additionalspecialty credential preferred.

Education Required:

  • Completion of advanced training through a recognized or accredited program, equivalent in scope and rigor to post-secondary education or equivalent knowledge. High school diploma or GED required.

Experience Required:

  • Typically requires 4 years of experience in expert-level professional coding.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required:

  • Advanced Coding Expertise: In-depth knowledge of ICD, CPT, and HCPCS coding guidelines, ensuring accurate and compliant coding practices.
  • Medical Terminology & Anatomy: Strong understanding of medical terminology, anatomy, and physiology to support precise code assignment.
  • Epic & Reporting Solutions: Advanced knowledge of Epic and other reporting tools to analyze data, generate reports, and optimize workflow efficiencies.
  • Critical Thinking & Analytical Skills: Highly proficient in problem-solving and analytical thinking with strong attention to detail.
  • Interpersonal Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to educate and collaborate effectively with physicians, APCs, clinical leadership, and coding teams.
  • Advanced Computer Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, electronic coding applications, and email communication.
  • Organizational & Prioritization Skills: Ability to efficiently manage multiple tasks, set priorities, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Independent Decision-Making: Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and make informed decisions regarding coding and compliance.
  • Collaboration & Initiative: Strong ability to take initiative, contribute to process improvements, and work collaboratively within a team environment.

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:

  • Follow organizational and divisional remote work policy and guidelines.
  • Operates all equipment necessary to perform the job.
  • Handles a fast paced and creative work environment moving independently from one task to another.
  • Makes sound decisions within limited time frames and always conducts business in a professional manner and has demonstrates ability to work cooperatively and effectively with others on an individual and team basis.

This job description indicates the general nature and level of work expected of the incumbent. It is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the incumbent. Incumbent may be required to perform other related duties.

About Advocate Health

Advocate Health is the third-largest nonprofit, integrated health system in the United States, created from the combination of Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health. Providing care under the names Advocate Health Care in Illinois; Atrium Health in the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama; and Aurora Health Care in Wisconsin, Advocate Health is a national leader in clinical innovation, health outcomes, consumer experience and value-based care. title: Southeast (SE) Cohort Project Manager – Distressed Borrowers Assistance Network
description:

Reporting to the DBAN Project Manager, this role includes supervision of DSPs, training coordination in concert with subject matter experts and DBAN partners, operations, and event planning (for gatherings and trainings) for a regional cohort within a national network that ensures farmers receive informed, dignified, and timely assistance navigating USDA programs and financial crises.

  • Self-starter: can take initiative both on projects and work plans, and seek information independently

  • Experience working in the U.S. Southeast

  • Experience with USDA programs, farm finance, or agricultural policy

Compensation: Full-time salaried, exempt position. Annual salary of $60,889.00 based on 40 hours/week. Generous benefits package includes paid time off, 401k, medical, dental, life insurance, and long/short-term disability insurance plans.

  • This position is funded by a federal grant until June 2027. Grant-funded positions are contingent upon continued funding and on grant renewal.

Location: Remote (applicants based in NC, SC, VA, MS preferred) Applicants must be within one time zone of Eastern Standard Time.

In your cover letter, please explain why you are interested in RAFI and how your experience prepares you to support farmers and advocates in the Southeast. Please no calls or emails.

title: Director, Integrated Business Testing
description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

Job Summary:

The Director, Integrated Business Testing is accountable for ensuring that business transformation initiatives are thoroughly validated, business‑ready, and fit for operational use prior to deployment. This role establishes and governs enterprise testing strategy, ensuring solutions meet business requirements, support critical operations, and minimize disruption at go‑live. The Testing Lead partners closely with Program Leads, business stakeholders, and enablement teams to ensure real‑world scenarios are tested and validated. This role also plays a critical role in managing quality risk and building confidence in deployment readiness.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Define and own the enterprise testing strategy across transformation initiatives, aligned to business readiness and risk tolerance.
  • Establish testing standards, approaches, and governance for functional, integration, and business‑scenario testing.
  • Partner with Program Leads to define testing scope, priorities, and success criteria.
  • Ensure robust business participation in testing activities, including representation of real‑world scenarios, peak volumes, and exception cases.
  • Coordinate testing schedules and dependencies across multiple concurrent initiatives.
  • Monitor test execution progress, defect trends, and quality indicators; escalate risks as needed.
  • Ensure issues identified during testing are clearly prioritized, tracked, and resolved.
  • Partner with Process Redesign, OCM, and Training teams to validate readiness from an end‑to‑end business perspective.
  • Support go‑live decision‑making by providing clear, data‑driven assessments of readiness and residual risk.
  • Participate in cutover planning and readiness checkpoints to ensure testing outcomes support deployment decisions.
  • Capture lessons learned and continuously improve testing practices across waves.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Experience & Education:

  • Minimum of 10–12 years of experience leading testing, quality assurance, or readiness activities for large‑scale transformation initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience in leading validation/Testing effort for complex, cross‑functional solutions for large scale enterprise wide transformation
  • Strong experience working with business stakeholders to define and validate testing scenarios.
  • Proven ability to manage risk, quality, and readiness in high‑visibility programs.
  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

Minimum Skills, Knowledge, & Abilities:

  • Strong understanding of enterprise testing strategies and quality management principles.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into effective testing approaches.
  • Excellent analytical skills to assess readiness, quality trends, and risk exposure.
  • Proven ability to influence program and business leaders on readiness and risk decisions.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to convey testing outcomes to executive audiences.
  • High attention to detail balanced with enterprise‑level perspective.

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to operate in a dynamic, time‑bound (3–5 year) transformation environment.
  • Ability to support extended hours during testing cycles and deployment readiness windows.
  • Travel as required to support key testing events and readiness reviews.
